Convert Temporal values to base R dates and times

Source: R/base-r.R
base-r.Rd

Methods for base R's as.Date(), as.POSIXct() and as.POSIXlt(), and temporal_to_difftime(), which stands in for as.difftime() because base R's is not a generic (design 6.10). The other direction is the constructors: plain_date(<Date>), instant(<POSIXct>), zoned_date_time(<POSIXct>), plain_date_time(<POSIXct>), plain_time(<difftime>) and duration(<difftime>).

Usage

# S3 method for class 'zutempo_plain_date'
as.Date(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'zutempo_plain_date_time'
as.Date(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'zutempo_zoned_date_time'
as.Date(x, tz = NULL, ...)

# S3 method for class 'zutempo_instant'
as.Date(x, tz = "UTC", ...)

# S3 method for class 'zutempo_instant'
as.POSIXct(x, tz = "UTC", ...)

# S3 method for class 'zutempo_zoned_date_time'
as.POSIXct(x, tz = NULL, ...)

# S3 method for class 'zutempo_plain_date_time'
as.POSIXct(x, tz, ..., disambiguation = "compatible")

# S3 method for class 'zutempo_zoned_date_time'
as.POSIXlt(x, tz = NULL, ...)

# S3 method for class 'zutempo_instant'
as.POSIXlt(x, tz = "UTC", ...)

# S3 method for class 'zutempo_plain_date_time'
as.POSIXlt(x, tz, ..., disambiguation = "compatible")

temporal_to_difftime(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'zutempo_plain_time'
temporal_to_difftime(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'zutempo_duration'
temporal_to_difftime(x, ..., relative_to = NULL)

Arguments

x

A zutempo value.

...

Must be empty.

tz

A time zone: for an instant(), the zone to show it in (the default is "UTC"); for a plain_date_time(), the zone its wall-clock time is in, which has no default ("" is the system zone); for a zoned_date_time(), a zone to show it in instead of its own.

disambiguation

For a plain_date_time(): how to resolve a time a zone skips or repeats, as in temporal_to_zoned_date_time().

relative_to

For a duration() with years, months or weeks: the date or zoned date-time they count from, as in temporal_total().

Value

A Date, POSIXct, POSIXlt or difftime (in seconds), NA where x is NA.

Details

What each conversion loses:

  • plain_date() to Date: nothing; both count days from 1970-01-01.

  • instant() to POSIXct: the nanoseconds, to the nearest double second (ties to even), which keeps about 240 ns at today's dates. The other way takes the double's exact value, rounded half to even to the nanosecond, so 0.1 s is 100 ms.

  • zoned_date_time() to POSIXct: as instant(), with the zone as tzone. A vector mixing zones gets "UTC", and so does a fixed offset that is not a whole number of hours, which base R cannot name; a whole-hour offset becomes its Etc/GMT zone.

  • zoned_date_time() to POSIXlt: the fields in each element's own zone, with its offset in gmtoff; the seconds lose precision as above.

  • plain_date_time() to POSIXct or POSIXlt: needs tz, and resolves a wall-clock time a zone skips or repeats with disambiguation, as temporal_to_zoned_date_time() does.

  • instant(), zoned_date_time() and plain_date_time() to Date: the date, in tz for an instant().

  • plain_time() to difftime: seconds since midnight, as a double.

  • duration() to difftime: its total in seconds, as temporal_total() gives it, so years, months and weeks need relative_to and a day is 24 hours without it.

plain_year_month() and plain_month_day() have no base R counterpart; temporal_to_plain_date() supplies the missing day or year first.

Examples

as.Date(plain_date("2026-03-07"))
#> [1] "2026-03-07"
as.POSIXct(instant("2026-03-07T12:00:00.123456789Z"))
#> [1] "2026-03-07 12:00:00 UTC"
as.POSIXct(zoned_date_time("2026-03-07T12:00[Europe/Lisbon]"))
#> [1] "2026-03-07 12:00:00 WET"
as.POSIXlt(zoned_date_time("2026-03-07T12:00[Europe/Lisbon]"))
#> [1] "2026-03-07 12:00:00 WET"
as.POSIXct(plain_date_time("2026-03-29T01:30"), tz = "Europe/Lisbon")
#> [1] "2026-03-29 02:30:00 WEST"
temporal_to_difftime(plain_time("12:30"))
#> Time difference of 45000 secs
temporal_to_difftime(duration("P1M"), relative_to = "2026-02-01")
#> Time difference of 2419200 secs

# And back.
plain_date(as.Date("2026-03-07"))
#> <zutempo_plain_date[1]>
#> [1] 2026-03-07
instant(as.POSIXct("2026-03-07 12:00:00", tz = "UTC"))
#> <zutempo_instant[1]>
#> [1] 2026-03-07T12:00:00Z
duration(as.difftime(90, units = "mins"))
#> <zutempo_duration[1]>
#> [1] PT5400S
